_doc: Reviewed monotone constraints for XGBoost. +1 = a higher value may only raise (never lower) predicted risk; -1 = a higher value may only lower it. Only features with an unambiguous economic direction are listed. Columns are the dataset's own 0-1 normalised ratios; winsorising and RobustScaler are order-preserving, so these directions survive preprocessing.

Debt ratio %.reason: More debt per unit of assets = more leverage.

Current Liability to Assets.reason: More short-term obligations per unit of assets.

Current Liability to Current Assets.reason: Inverse of the current ratio: less liquidity.

Net worth/Assets.reason: Equity cushion (= 1 - Debt ratio % in this data).

Equity to Liability.reason: More equity per unit of liabilities.

excluded_on_purpose.Interest Coverage Ratio (Interest expens: Name is contradictory: 'coverage' (EBIT/interest, higher = safer) vs 'interest expense to EBIT' (higher = riskier). The direction cannot be verified from the dataset documentation.
excluded_on_purpose.Interest Expense Ratio: Rank correlation with bankruptcy is negative (-0.13), the opposite of what the name suggests, so the normalisation is unclear.
excluded_on_purpose.Degree of Financial Leverage (DFL): Sign depends on whether EBIT is positive; ambiguous after normalisation.
excluded_on_purpose.growth rates (all): Fast growth can be healthy or a sign of over-expansion.
excluded_on_purpose.Operating Gross Margin and other margin: Plausibly -1, but left free to limit the metric cost; profitability is already constrained through ROA and net income.
